info.title: arr-metadata-server
info.description:
A self-hosted metadata server for the *arr stack.

It answers three client protocols from one store — Sonarr's Skyhook API, Radarr's metadata API, and the TMDB v3 API — alongside its own API, documented here in full, and it is a metadata provider Plex Media Server can be given, under `/plex`. TheTVDB's v4 API and AniList's are relayed to the real services, with the fields locked here written into their answers.

**Locks.** Any field a person edits is recorded separately from provider data and is never overwritten by a refresh. That is what the `/items/{id}/overrides` routes manage, and what `lockedFields` reports.

**Authentication differs per surface.** Sonarr and Radarr have their metadata URLs compiled in and cannot attach a credential, and Plex sends none to a provider, so those routes are guarded by address rather than by key. The routes documented without a security requirement are those; they are not open.

get.summary:
Relay any TMDB v3 request, with this server's locks written in on the way
back.
get.description:
The request goes upstream with this server's own credentials substituted
for whatever the client sent — or, when `tmdb.relayCredential` is
`client`, with the client's own TMDB key or token as it came, a key issued
here being refused with a 401 that says why. If the path addresses a
title a person locked fields on, those fields are written into the
upstream document before it is returned, so the client gets TMDB's full
response with the operator's corrections in it. A text — a title, an
overview — is written as it is locked for the language the client asked
(`language=`, TMDB's `en-US` when none is): locked in that language, or in
every one. One locked in another language alone leaves TMDB's own text in
the one asked.

Every TMDB v3 path is accepted; see TMDB's own documentation for their
shapes. Patched: `/3/movie/{id}`, `/3/tv/{id}`, `/3/tv/{id}/season/{n}`,
`/3/tv/{id}/season/{n}/episode/{e}`, and the results of
`/3/search/{movie,tv,multi}`, `/3/trending/{movie,tv,all}/{window}` and
`/3/discover/{movie,tv}`.

get.summary:
What airs and what comes out in a window: the episodes of every series,
and the films out in cinemas, digitally or on disc.
get.description:
An episode by the moment it airs, in UTC — where no provider knew the
time, midnight UTC on its date, which is what Sonarr is given; a release
by its day, at midnight UTC too, once for each day a film comes out. A
film's days are the reader's country's where its releases there are
known, its own otherwise, and a day somebody corrected by hand stays as
they put it. The window is the caller's to choose, so a day is the
caller's own day wherever it is. Switched off, or for adults where the
reader would not be shown one, a work is left out of both.

get.summary: A Kometa metadata file of the corrections locked here.
get.description:
For Plex libraries run by [Kometa](https://kometa.wiki): a `metadata:` file
with an entry for each work that has something locked — matched by TMDB id
(films) or TheTVDB id (series), by IMDb id where it has not that one —
carrying *only* what was locked: title, sort title, original title, summary,
tagline, first release, content rating, studio, genres, the poster and
background chosen, and for a series its seasons' titles, summaries and
posters and its episodes' titles, summaries and dates. Kometa puts them over
what Plex's agent found, on every run.

Name it under `metadata_files` of the library — as a file saved from here,
or by this address with `?apikey=` and the key of an editor or an
administrator, which is what asking for it takes: a key limited to the
`read` scope will do, since Kometa only reads. A key that belongs to nobody
needs the `write` scope.

parameters.description:
`movie` or `series`. A metadata file belongs to one library and a
library holds one kind: films are matched by TMDB id, series by

The language of the library, `fr` or `fra`: texts locked for it, and
for every language, are written; those locked for another are not.
Left out, the language the catalogue is kept in.

post.summary:
Write a `.nfo` document for everything, under `AMS_NFO_EXPORT_PATH` — or,
with `?list=`, for the works of one selection.
post.description:
The layout is `series/{slug}/tvshow.nfo`, `series/{slug}/Season NN/SNNENN.nfo`
and `movies/{slug}/movie.nfo`. That directory structure is this server's own:
nothing here can know how your library is laid out, so the files land
somewhere predictable for you to copy or link from.

Answered at once, and written in the background: a library's artwork is
thousands of downloads — One Piece alone has a still for each of more than
a thousand episodes — and a request is cut off after a minute, which used
to stop the export wherever it had got to. The run is a job; its record
says when it is done and what it wrote.

get.summary:
Relay any TheTVDB v4 read, with this server's locks written in on the way
back.
get.description:
A bearer token that is a key issued here is this server's business: the
operator's own TheTVDB token takes its place, and the client's copy never
leaves. Any other token is the client's own, and travels as it came. A
caller with no token who authenticated with a key — in the header or the
query — is asked for with the operator's token too. The operator's own
account, `user` and what hangs off it, is nobody else's: refused with
the operator's token, read with a client's own. With each client's own
key relayed (`tvdb.relayCredential = client`), the operator's token is
never used, and a key issued here is refused with a 401 that says why.

Every v4 path is accepted; see TheTVDB's own documentation for their
shapes. The documents about a work of this catalogue are the ones patched:
`series/{id}` and `movies/{id}`, both `/extended` — with the translations,
seasons and episodes asked with them — and `/translations/{lang}`; a page
of a series' episodes in any of its orders, `[/{lang}]`; `seasons/{id}`
and its `/extended`; one episode, `/extended` and `/translations/{lang}`.

cancelable.description: Whether a run in progress can be stopped.

blocked.description: Why it cannot be run now, when it cannot.

error.description: What went wrong, in the words of the check that failed.

issuer.description: The issuer to try; the stored one when left out.

noPoster.description:
Works with no poster: no image of that kind of their own, and none
chosen by hand to lead.

noOverview.description:
Works with no overview in the language they are stored in — none given,
or one cleared by hand; one written by hand, in that language or in
every one, is an overview.

neverRefreshed.description:
Works never refreshed that have an identifier elsewhere to refresh by.
A work entered by hand is never refreshed, and is not one of these.

expiringKeys.description: Keys, still switched on, that stop working within `keyHorizonDays`.

keyHorizonDays.description: How many days ahead a key's end is counted.

failedMedia.description: Pictures and themes every try at fetching failed for.

tagline.description:
The line under the title in this language, where the source gives
one: TMDB does, in each of its translations.

TvdbLoginRequest.description: What a TheTVDB client signs in with.

apikey.description: A key issued here, or the client's own TheTVDB key.

pin.description: A subscriber's PIN, with the client's own key.

Unavailable.description: Why a provider cannot be asked about a work now.

UpdateAvailable.description: A release newer than the version running.

oidcLinked.description: Whether an identity provider vouches for this account.

hasPassword.description: Whether the account has a password of its own to sign in with.

ValueSource.description: Who gave one value, and who else had a say.

from.description: The provider whose value was kept.

agreed.description: Others that gave the same value.

differed.description: Others that gave another value, and lost to it.

passed.description:
Those ahead of it in priority that gave none: why a lower source's
value stands. Sources that describe nothing — artwork alone — are not
counted, or every field would name them.

logo.description: The service's mark, as TMDB serves it.

Web.description: The interface's and the native API's door.

tls.description: Whether it is in TLS, from the operator's files.

WebhookDeliveries.description: A page of a destination's log.

total.description: How many the log holds: thirty days of it, the newest thousand.

WebhookDelivery.description: One event owed to a destination, and how its tries went.

attempts.description: The tries made, of the eight it gets.

nextAttemptAt.description: When it is tried next, while it waits.

lastStatus.description: What the address answered the last try with, when it answered.

lastError.description: Why the last try was not taken, in words that name no address.

durationMs.description: How long the last try took, in milliseconds.

replayOf.description: The delivery this one sends again, when it is a replay.

oneOf.description: What it tells.

WebhookDeliveryCounts.description: How many deliveries of each standing a destination's log holds.

WebhookDestination.description:
A destination, as the administration sees it: never its secret, and its
address with what follows the host masked.

address.description:
Its address: the scheme, host and port shown, the rest masked — for
most services the token is in the path.

secretSet.description:
Whether a secret is kept: a standard destination's signing secret,
an ntfy or Gotify one's token. Never sent back.

secret.description:
The signing secret just made, in the answer that made it and in no
other: it cannot be read again, only made anew.

events.description: The events it is told of; `*` for every one.

grouped.description:
Whether failed refreshes are told to it together: a few minutes'
worth in one message, counted by cause, rather than one per work.

disabledReason.description:
Why the server switched it off, when it did: an address that
answered 410 Gone.

WebhookDestinationInput.description:
A destination to make, or what to change of one: each field left out
stays as it is.

address.description:
Where it is posted: a webhook's address, an ntfy topic's, a Gotify
server's, an Apprise API's `/notify/{key}`. Left out or empty on a
change, the address kept stays.

token.description:
The token an ntfy topic or a Gotify application was given: left out,
the one kept stays — while the destination stays the same kind at the
same origin, its address's scheme, host and port; moved to another
kind or origin, it is dropped unless given again. Empty, it is
removed. Never sent back. A standard destination's signing secret is
made here instead, and made anew at another origin.

events.description:
The events it is told of; `*` for every one. Left out on a new one,
what enters and leaves the catalogue.

grouped.description:
Whether failed refreshes are told to it together: a few minutes'
worth in one message, counted by cause. Left out on a new one, on for
the kinds people read — discord, slack, ntfy, gotify, apprise — and
off for standard and json, read by programs that want an event per
work; left out on a change, it stays as it is.

WebhookEvents.description: Every name a destination can be told of, besides `*`.

facts.description:
What happens on its own: a refresh failed, a medium given up on, a
newer release out.

actions.description: The actions of the audit trail, in the order its filter offers them.

defaults.description: What a new destination is told of, until other events are ticked.

kinds.description: The kinds of destination, in the order they are offered.

WebhookMessage.description:
One thing told, as a delivery keeps it: the event, who did it, to what,
what is worth saying of it, and when.

count.description:
How many things it tells of together — failed refreshes grouped for
a destination — when there are more than one.

WebhookTest.description: What a test of a destination came to.

delivered.description: Whether the address took it: it answered, with a success.

status.description: What it answered with, when it answered.

error.description:
Why it was not reached, or what it said when it refused — in words
that name no address.

refused.description:
Why nothing was sent: `not_web`, not an http(s) address or one that
names this machine; `internal`, a name that resolves to an address
only reachable from here; `unsent`, the post could not be made — a
standard destination without its secret — as `error` says.

millis.description: How long it took, in milliseconds.

link.description:
TMDB's page for the work in that country, which carries JustWatch's
own links to each service.

free.description: Free to watch, and free with advertising.

regions.description: Every country TMDB lists anything for, so a reader may ask for another.

attribution.description: Who the data comes from; shown beside it, as TMDB's terms ask.

WorkMedia.description: A work's media, and whether anything is kept at all.

store.description:
Whether a store is configured: without one, nothing can be uploaded
and nothing is fetched.

WorkMedium.description: One address a work points at, and what is kept of it.

url.description: Where it is read from now: the copy kept, or the provider.

status.description:
`stored`, `pending`, `failed` — or `absent`, when nothing has been
asked of it: the store is off, or the address is not one it fetches.

WorkRef.description: A work named in passing — by an audit entry, a job — as a reader knows it.
